WHAT YOU SHOULD KNOW ABOUT FILING A CIVIL RIGHTS OR 
HEALTH INFORMATION PRIVACY COMPLAINT WITH THE 
OFFICE FOR CIVIL RIGHTS (OCR)

OCR'S ROLE
OCR investigates complaints that an entity or its employees discriminated 
against you or someone else on the basis of race, color, national origin, 
disability, age, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and 
gender identity), or religion.

OCR also investigates complaints that an entity or its employees violated 
your health information privacy or security rights under the Health 
Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

OCR is a neutral investigator and does not represent you or the entity.

THE COMPLAINT PROCESS
1. Filing a complaint: You can file a complaint with OCR using our 
   online portal or by mail, fax, or email.
2. Reviewing your complaint: OCR will review your complaint to 
   determine if it has the legal authority to investigate and if the 
   complaint was filed on time.
3. Investigation: If OCR investigates your complaint, it will work 
   with you and the entity to gather information and determine if a 
   violation occurred.
4. Resolution: If OCR finds a violation, it will work with the entity 
   to correct the problem. If the entity does not correct the problem, 
   OCR may take further action, such as referring the case to the 
   Department of Justice.
